shared_elements: rectangular carved stone pillar/slab set upright in an excavated area
shallow low-relief carving on tan weathered limestone
quadruped animal shown in profile in low relief
repeated geometric motif filling a zone of the surface (lattice/net in A, rows of arches and hatched rectangles in B)
loose rubble and broken stone blocks surrounding the carved stone
a second, plainer stone block in the foreground
justification: Both show an upright rectangular limestone pillar carved in very shallow relief, with an abstract repeating geometric field occupying the upper part of the face and a profile quadruped placed lower down, amid excavation rubble and a plainer block in the foreground. The main difference is that B's ornament is organised into strict horizontal registers of arch and bar motifs with several figures including what may be a human-like form and a handled object, whereas A's ornament is a single irregular net-like mesh with one sparse animal, and A is shot from a wider, more oblique viewpoint showing walling behind.
